questions.q: India's rank in the world by area (total geographical area) is:
questions.explain: India covers about 3.28 million sq km and is the seventh largest country in the world.

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which Indian state?
questions.explain: It crosses 8 states — Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha is not one of them.

questions.q: The Standard Meridian of India, which fixes Indian Standard Time, is:
questions.explain: Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on 82.5°E longitude passing near Mirzapur (UP); India follows a single time zone.

questions.q: India shares its longest land border with:
questions.explain: India's longest land border (about 4,096 km) is with Bangladesh; the shortest is with Afghanistan.

questions.q: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary between India and:
questions.explain: The Radcliffe Line (1947) divides India and Pakistan; McMahon Line = India-China, Durand Line = Pakistan-Afghanistan.

questions.q: The McMahon Line separates India from:
questions.explain: The McMahon Line is the boundary between India (Arunachal Pradesh) and China.

questions.q: The largest state of India by area is:
questions.explain: Rajasthan is the largest state; Madhya Pradesh is second.

questions.q: The smallest state of India by area is:
questions.explain: Goa is the smallest state by area, though Sikkim has the smallest population.

questions.q: The longest river of India (flowing within the country) is the:
questions.explain: The Ganga is India's longest river; the Brahmaputra is longer overall but flows mostly outside India.

questions.q: The largest tributary of the Ganga is the:
questions.explain: The Yamuna joins the Ganga at Prayagraj (Sangam) and is its biggest tributary.

questions.q: The longest river of peninsular India, called 'Dakshin Ganga', is the:
questions.explain: The Godavari (about 1,465 km) rises at Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra, and is called the Ganga of the South.

questions.q: The Narmada river is known for flowing:
options: Eastwards to the Bay of Bengal
questions.explain: Narmada and Tapi flow west through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea and form estuaries, not deltas.

questions.q: In Tibet, the Brahmaputra river is known by the name:
questions.explain: It is Tsangpo in Tibet, Siang/Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, Brahmaputra in Assam and Jamuna in Bangladesh.

questions.q: The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) was signed between India and:
questions.explain: Under the 1960 treaty, the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) went mainly to India and the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) mainly to Pakistan.

questions.q: The height of Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, is about:
questions.explain: Everest (Nepal-Tibet border) is 8,848.86 m; K2 is 8,611 m and Kangchenjunga 8,586 m.

questions.q: The highest mountain peak located entirely within India's territory is:
questions.explain: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m, Sikkim-Nepal border) is India's highest peak; Nanda Devi is the highest entirely inside India.

questions.q: Nathu La, a famous mountain pass on the India-China border, is located in:
questions.explain: Nathu La connects Sikkim with Tibet and is a border trade route.

questions.q: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explain: Gujarat's highly indented coast (about 1,600 km) is the longest among Indian states.

questions.q: Black soil (regur), found in the Deccan plateau, is best suited for:
questions.explain: Black soil holds moisture well and is ideal for cotton — hence it is also called black cotton soil.

questions.q: The most fertile and most widespread soil of India, covering the northern plains, is:
questions.explain: Alluvial soil, deposited by rivers, covers the largest area and supports most of India's farming.

questions.q: Rice, maize, cotton and groundnut, sown with the onset of the monsoon, are examples of:
questions.explain: Kharif crops are sown in June-July and harvested in September-October; wheat and mustard are Rabi crops.

questions.q: Wheat, mustard and gram, sown in winter, are examples of:
questions.explain: Rabi crops are sown in October-November and harvested in spring.

questions.q: About 75% of India's annual rainfall is received from the:
questions.explain: The SW monsoon (June-September) brings roughly three-fourths of India's total rain.

questions.q: The Tamil Nadu coast receives most of its rainfall from the:
questions.explain: In October-December the retreating NE monsoon picks up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and rains on the Coromandel coast.

questions.q: The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, is formed in the delta of:
questions.explain: The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta (largely in West Bengal and Bangladesh) is the world's largest delta and home to the Sundarbans.

questions.q: Chilika Lake, India's largest coastal lagoon, is located in:
questions.explain: Chilika is a brackish-water lagoon on the Odisha coast, famous for migratory birds.

questions.q: Wular Lake, one of the largest freshwater lakes of Asia, is in:
questions.explain: Wular Lake is formed by the Jhelum river in Kashmir.

questions.q: Loktak Lake, famous for its floating islands (phumdis), is located in:
questions.explain: Loktak in Manipur hosts Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park.

questions.q: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, lies mainly in:
questions.explain: Most of the Thar spreads over western Rajasthan.

questions.q: Anaimudi, the highest peak of South India, is located in the:
questions.explain: Anaimudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest point of peninsular India.

questions.q: The Eastern and Western Ghats meet at the:
questions.explain: The two Ghats join at the Nilgiri Hills, where Doddabetta is a well-known peak.

questions.q: The Kaveri river rises from:
questions.explain: The Kaveri originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri range of Karnataka and flows to Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: The Krishna river originates near:
questions.explain: Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats; Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar and Narmada at Amarkantak.

questions.q: The Bhakra Nangal Dam, one of India's highest gravity dams, is built on the river:
questions.explain: Bhakra Dam stands on the Sutlej in Himachal Pradesh; its reservoir is called Gobind Sagar.

questions.q: The Hirakud Dam, among the longest dams in the world, is built across the:
questions.explain: Hirakud (Odisha) is built on the Mahanadi river.

questions.q: The Tehri Dam, India's tallest dam, is built on the river:
questions.explain: Tehri Dam (Uttarakhand) stands on the Bhagirathi, a headstream of the Ganga.

questions.q: Jog Falls, one of India's highest waterfalls, is formed by the river:
questions.explain: Jog Falls in Karnataka is created by the Sharavathi river dropping about 253 m.

questions.q: Majuli, one of the world's largest river islands, is located in the river:
questions.explain: Majuli island lies in the Brahmaputra in Assam and is a centre of Assamese Vaishnavite culture.

questions.q: The Atal Tunnel, which provides all-weather connectivity to Lahaul, passes under which pass?
questions.explain: The 9.02 km Atal Tunnel (2020) runs under the Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh.

questions.q: India's latitudinal extent is roughly from:
questions.explain: Mainland India stretches from about 8°4'N (near Kanyakumari) to 37°6'N in the north.
